races.name: Virgin Bet / EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cubbie's Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Jonathan Portman who was beaten nine lengths on debut at Goodwood over this course and distance; Rob Hornby retains the ride but she was noted fading late, making her reliant on a stronger pace than this small field is likely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Cut And Sew
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly raced filly has two Goodwood starts to her name and placed over 5f here, giving her the most course experience of the hold-up types; Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking but her off-pace style is compromised by the lone-leader tempo expected.|

runners_data.name: Gobby Grace
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes debutante with no public form to assess; Hector Crouch takes the ride on going classed as good to firm which Hughes handles well on debut, making her the chief wildcard if she has natural speed, though her optimal style is entirely unknown.|

runners_data.name: Motown Filly
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Richard Spencer who has shaped with some promise, finishing second on soft ground at Goodwood over 6f; she is the only horse likely to share early ground with Queen Of Christmas and fast conditions are a query after that soft-ground placing.|

runners_data.name: Queen Of Christmas
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's front-runner has two starts over 5f at Goodwood and now steps up to 6f, which may actually suit her better given her tendency to be headed late at the minimum trip; Pierre-Louis Jamin is an astute booking on a leader who will enjoy a completely uncontested lead.|

runners_data.name: Wig Wam Bam
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Jack Channon who finished eighth on her sole start over 6f at Goodwood; Tom Marquand is an experienced jockey who will look to position her closer than her debut suggests, but fading late is a documented concern and the solo pace scenario makes her task harder.|

races.paceDynamic: Queen Of Christmas is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful pace rival to push her, she will stride into a clear lead from the break and control every fraction on this straight Goodwood 6f. Motown Filly is the only prominent-style runner and may track in second, but she lacks the pace or intent to seriously pressurise Queen Of Christmas, leaving the leader to dictate a steady, controlled tempo. The remaining four runners — Cubbie's Dream, Wig Wam Bam, Cut And Sew, and Gobby Grace — all sit in midfield or hold-up positions and will be chasing from off the pace against a leader who has had a soft lead throughout. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up and late-running profiles if the pace is falsely slow, but on a straight 6f at Goodwood where leaders with a clear advantage can sustain their momentum to the line, the most likely beneficiary is Queen Of Christmas herself or any prominent racer close enough to pounce in the final furlong without having to make up excessive ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queen Of Christmas Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Of Christmas dictates an unchallenged lead and maintains gallop through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With no pace rival to force a genuine tempo, she sets every fraction to suit herself and the straight 6f at Goodwood favours a leader who can roll through the line on fast ground without being asked an awkward question mid-race. Hold-up horses will need the pace to be genuinely strong to reel her in, and with only Motown Filly remotely close in the early stages, that pressure never materialises.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Swamps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to stretch the field and one of the hold-up fillies produces a strong sustained finish in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Cubbie's Dream or Wig Wam Bam would need to be positioned within striking range turning into the straight, as a 6f Goodwood dash does not allow a deep hold-up horse to close enormous ground in the final stages. The fast ground suits a filly with a good finishing kick, but the solo leader scenario makes this outcome genuinely secondary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante Gobby Grace Impresses
scenarios.trigger: If Gobby Grace, on debut for Richard Hughes, shows natural tactical speed and slots into contention early enough to challenge.
scenarios.body: Hughes regularly has his debutants sharp and ready, and a 6f Goodwood sprint gives a well-drilled newcomer the chance to show natural speed without needing to come from off the pace. With the going good to firm and the trip likely to suit an athletic type on first appearance, she is the unknown quantity who could reshape the outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Cut And Sew Improves Sharply
scenarios.trigger: If Cut And Sew's two prior runs at Goodwood prove a springboard for a significant step forward under Kieran Shoemark.
scenarios.body: She has course experience and placed on one visit, and Ed Walker's lightly raced fillies can improve markedly at this stage of the season, but her style leaves her dependent on a strong pace that this race is unlikely to generate. A breakthrough is possible but against the grain of the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Queen Of Christmas — watch her break from the stalls; if she jumps cleanly and Pierre-Louis Jamin allows her to bowl along at her own rhythm, the solo lead she secures will be very difficult to reel in over this straight 6f on fast ground.

Gobby Grace — Richard Hughes debuts are often well-prepared and if she shows natural early speed she could slot into second or third and pose a genuine late threat; her unknown style makes her the biggest X-factor in the race.

Motown Filly — if George Wood asks her to close the gap on Queen Of Christmas before halfway rather than sitting passively, she could inject just enough tempo to bring the hold-up fillies into the race in the final furlong.

Cubbie's Dream and Wig Wam Bam — both are noted as faders in their only starts and both face the same task from off the pace; watch whether either is positioned closer than expected, as a genuine hold-up run from this controlled pace is unlikely to deliver a winning finish.

races.name: White & Brooks Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shady Bay
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with solid course form at Goodwood (won over 10f here), runs prominently and is well placed in a race of this nature; 18 days since last run is fine, but needs to find improvement on recent efforts to beat the top of the market.
runners_data.comment: Shady Bay caught the eye with a close second last time out and has placed three times in her last four starts, bringing solid recent consistency to this contest; the main risk is whether she can convert that form into victory, having managed just the one win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Grace Harris in good form (5 from 15 over 14 days) and has placed well at Goodwood multiple times; her natural instinct is to race close to the pace but with so many prominent types in this field she is likely to find herself in a more rearward position than she would prefer, which undermines her chance.
runners_data.comment: Oasis Sunrise has experience of today's trip and going, and her recent record shows a third two starts back to go alongside two wins in her last six, though a fourth last time out leaves her needing to find a little more from stall two carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing blinkers, but Goodwood form figures of 6-2-3-6 give minimal confidence he can dominate; Ralph Beckett's runner has a 39-day freshener and limited winning form, and will need to lead clearly to show his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Molo Del Palazzo does bring placed efforts into the mix — a second two starts back and a third three starts back — yet that sixth last time out after 39 days off gives pause, and carrying 135 lb from stall 12 adds to the ask.

runners_data.name: Blue Noon
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon-trained with Goodwood course form across six of her last seven runs, and multiple placed efforts at this track on identical ground; has a frustrating streak of seconds but is consistent enough to be competitive from a prominent position if the pace suits.
runners_data.comment: Blue Noon has been knocking at the door, finishing second two starts back and second last time out, with experience over today's trip and going and a rating that has her sharing top spot — yet to score in recent starts and a trainer in worrying form at just 4% over the past fortnight are the risks to factor in.

runners_data.name: Hauteluce
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark rides a horse with a fine recent profile — two wins in her last four including a Goodwood placed effort — and drops back from a hold-up role into a race where the pace is likely to be fair; only one similar-going run on record here, but Ed Walker's filly has been in excellent form.
runners_data.comment: Hauteluce won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims, though she carries 135 lb from stall one and ranked seventh of thirteen on our ratings suggests she faces a stiff test against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Blue Wonder
runners_data.note: David Egan on a genuine hold-up horse who won over 10f on soft ground last year; 76-day gap since last run is a flag and limited course and distance form, but at OR=68 in a competitive fillies' handicap, a strong late run from the rear is her only winning route.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, Blue Wonder brings solid recent form to a return after 76 days, and she has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 135 lb from stall three, her overall profile — underlined by a rating of 81 — makes her our selection here.

runners_data.name: Alice De Clare
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form with multiple wins including two over 10f at Goodwood, and Jonny Peate rides for a James Fanshawe yard in solid nick (5 from 22 over 14 days); prominent racer with the course form to land this if she can get a good position on a fair gallop.
runners_data.comment: Dual winner in her last three completed starts — the most recent coming just 15 days ago — Alice De Clare has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet that seventh two starts back tempers expectations, and she carries 135 lb from stall 10 as the eighth-ranked of thirteen runners.

runners_data.name: Star Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a patchy recent record — only one placing at Goodwood in eight course runs — and Denis Coakley holds a quiet yard strike rate; needs everything to fall right from the rear and the form figures suggest limited faith at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Star Of Dubai does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, and 32 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; however, a fifth last time out and no better than sixth in the three before that make her a tough sell from stall five carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Brighton Beach
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has won at Goodwood and is lightly raced with upside; Tom Marquand takes the ride, the trip looks manageable stepping up from 8f, and as a confirmed front-runner she is the most natural pace-setter in the field.
runners_data.comment: Brighton Beach won last time out but ranks 12th of 13 on our figures, making her hard to fancy in this grade; she has run over today's distance and going before, and the 27-day break suggests she arrives fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Lady Milton
runners_data.note: Goodwood specialist with multiple placed efforts at the course and consistent form in handicaps; Rob Hornby rides and she races prominently, meaning she needs to secure a good rail position early in a field with strong pace competition.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed form in recent starts — second two runs back and a winner five starts back — shows Lady Milton is hitting the line well, and she has experience of today's distance and going; the weight burden of 133 lb may be the one factor working against her.

runners_data.name: Kokoluna
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old has a 98-day absence which is the longest in the field and a note of caution; however she has course and distance form (won over 8f at Goodwood) and OR=72 gives her a fair weight, so peak fitness is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures and representing a trainer desperately out of form at just one winner from twenty-nine attempts in the last fortnight, Kokoluna is hard to fancy despite a win in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and returns from a 98-day absence.

runners_data.name: Mohaab
runners_data.note: Nicola Currie rides at the lightest weight in the field (123lbs), and this three-year-old has placed at Goodwood over 12f; recent form figures include a win on soft and some below-par efforts, and she races from hold-up, meaning she needs a strong gallop to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Mohaab has managed just one win in her last five starts, finishing seventh last time out, and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures she faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days since her last outing leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Time After Time
runners_data.note: Heather Main's four-year-old has winning course form and two wins to her name; her natural racing style is to be held up at the rear, and with the field's depth she is likely to find herself positioned even further back than usual, making a winning challenge harder to execute.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Time After Time faces a stiff ask, having finished no better than fourth in her last four starts; the one win from her recent runs feels distant, and nothing in the profile screams a turnaround, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 43-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Molo Del Palazzo and Brighton Beach are the two confirmed pace-setters in a 13-runner field over a flat 1m2f on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood, and their presence guarantees a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a tactical dawdle. Brighton Beach won last time out over shorter and will likely push hard for the rail lead, while Molo Del Palazzo has shown consistent front-running intent; between them they ensure the pace is honest and sustained throughout. The field contains more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Oasis Sunrise and Time After Time are natural front-to-prominent racers who will be shuffled back from their preferred positions, meaning the true midfield is likely to be congested and those types face an uphill task racing out of role. A contested, honest gallop on quick ground over this distance historically suits hold-up horses and genuine closers who can travel within themselves and pick up in the straight — the race shape therefore most favours horses that can settle mid-to-rear and produce a strong sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the dual pace-setters force a genuinely strong early tempo, burning off the prominent types who cannot hold position.
scenarios.body: Hauteluce and Blue Wonder, both genuine hold-up horses, can settle into a rhythm and unleash a sustained late run as the pace-setters tie each other up; the honest gallop on Good To Firm ground suits a horse that travels kindly and finishes strongly over the full 1m2f trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rail Grinds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not blistering, allowing a prominent type that secures a good-ground position to stay on dourly without being swept up.
scenarios.body: Alice De Clare has been in fine form with multiple recent wins and can sit just off the leaders in a handy spot, while Blue Noon and Lady Milton are proven at this course and distance and equally capable of grinding out a result from a prominent position on a fair gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Brighton Beach breaks sharply and secures a clear lead, with Molo Del Palazzo slotting in just behind rather than fighting for the front.
scenarios.body: Brighton Beach, trained by William Haggas and ridden by Tom Marquand, has won on this course and could exploit a split-second clean break to control fractions and quicken on the straight without being challenged; Molo Del Palazzo is the main threat from the same group if Brighton Beach fades late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a mid-division horse with residual energy delivers a powerful late challenge that splits the field.
scenarios.body: Kokoluna has course form and proven ability to pick up off a steady pace, and Mohaab's light weight at 123lbs gives her an advantage if the race becomes a sprint home; both can benefit if the leaders and hold-up horses neutralise each other in the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Brighton Beach versus Molo Del Palazzo for the early lead — if they fight hard for position through the first two furlongs, the pace could become hot enough to compromise both their finishing efforts and set the race up for Hauteluce or Blue Wonder from behind.

Oasis Sunrise is a natural front-runner likely to be shuffled back against her preferred style in this congested field — watch whether Ashley Lewis (3) attempts to push forward regardless, which could cause interference and crowding in the early stages.

Kokoluna's 98-day absence is the longest layoff in the race; if she shows any signs of rustiness early, Charles Bishop may need to niggle her along, which could undermine her usual prominent hold from midfield.

Alice De Clare carries a strong recent winning sequence into this but races off the same OR=75 as several rivals — watch whether Jonny Peate can get a clean, unobstructed run from a prominent position given the volume of horses expected to press forward early.

Time After Time, mapped to midfield despite being a genuine hold-up type, may find Edward Greatrex forced to accept an even deeper position than expected — discount her if the field fans wide in the straight and she has too much ground to make up.

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Kissmehoneyhoney
runners_data.note: Runs prominently and is the only horse in the race capable of making the running; Haggas/Marquand is a powerful combination and her Goodwood course form (1st and 2nd here) is notable, though her most recent win came on Soft ground and Good to Firm may subtly reduce her stamina reserves at this stiff trip — still the pivotal horse in the shape.|
runners_data.comment: Kissmehoneyhoney shaped well when runner-up last time out and was a winner three starts back, bringing solid recent form into this on a trip she has run over before; the main concern is the 142 lb she carries.

runners_data.name: Ammoony
runners_data.note: Strong course record at Goodwood including a win over 10f, now stepping to 1m4f for the first time which represents the key question; David Egan will be able to sit just behind the leader from the front of the prominent group, and the consistent form string (2-2-1-2) suggests she rarely runs a bad race on this type of surface.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in good heart, Ammoony appeals as the one to beat here — runner-up last time out and a winner the start before that, she has experience on today's going and arrives fresh enough after 30 days, with her rating of 86 putting her narrowly at the head of the rankings.

runners_data.name: Liveinthelight
runners_data.note: Three wins from her last four starts is outstanding form and Goodwood over 12f is a proven happy hunting ground; she is a hold-up horse by style and will need the pace to honestly test those in front — the concern is that with only one genuine front-runner in the field, the gallop may be too controlled for her finishing kick to fully materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Liveinthelight arrives in fine nick, winning twice before finishing third last time out, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the main risk is whether she can defy a burden of 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Kelly Burn
runners_data.note: Won here at Goodwood over this exact course and distance, which stands out immediately; she has been off 63 days but James Fanshawe sends fit horses and a prominent racing style means she should not get caught cold — the 14-day trainer strike rate (5/22) is decent and the trip/track combination is hard to ignore.|
runners_data.comment: Kelly Burn won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, but 63 days off the track raises a fitness query and her speed rating of 70 leaves her with ground to find on the pick of these.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Ralph Beckett's yard who has produced just one in-the-frame finish from three career starts, all on softer ground than today's Good to Firm; she switches to hold-up tactics here and the form offers little basis for confidence on this evidence, with the step up to 1m4f also unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Marianita faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and returns after a 32-day break, but those are slim hooks on which to hang a case.

runners_data.name: Mother Dear
runners_data.note: Won over 10f at Goodwood last time she was effective on this track, but that was back among earlier form; she's been off 59 days, Hughie Morrison's 14-day record reads 0/7, and her three-run form string (8-1-5) is inconsistent — the going and trip are not certain problems, but the trainer form and layoff are mild flags.|
runners_data.comment: Mother Dear won two starts back but was well held fifth last time out, and the 59-day absence adds an element of doubt; she has the weight to carry at 127 lb, though our rating of 78 suggests she retains ability if bouncing back to her best.

runners_data.name: Pierpoint
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old has a genuine hold-up style in her bones, and her recent form (9-10-4-7) has been largely below expectations; she is placed into midfield on the pace map because the field houses too many closers for all to race from the rear, but her true preference is for a strong end-to-end gallop that does not look like materialising here — 42 days off and modest Goodwood form compound the concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, including a ninth most recently, Pierpoint faces a stiff ask here, and a trainer striking at just 4% over the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence; going experience is in her favour, but she rates a difficult one to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Cracking Beauty
runners_data.note: Has posted back-to-back third-place finishes including one at Goodwood over 12f, showing honest consistency at the track and trip; a natural hold-up operator whose best chance depends on a genuine pace developing, and with the race likely to be run at a measured tempo, her ability to close late may be partially blunted — Roger Teal's 14-day form (3/12) is respectable.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Cracking Beauty faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and back-to-back thirds show she can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Has course form at Goodwood (won over 12f there), handles this trip well, and Saffie Osborne has ridden her before; she carries a prominent-to-midfield style that will see her in a decent early position without fuss, and her recent form is consistent enough to suggest she is capable of being involved if the race plays into her hands.|
runners_data.comment: Glenna arrives on the back of a win two starts back and was third last time out, bringing strong recent form into this, and her experience over today's trip and going counts for plenty at 124 lb — though whether she can find more off an official 70 remains the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Kissmehoneyhoney is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, she will control pace through the first mile of this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood — a course that rewards those who can dictate a sustainable tempo from the front. Ammoony, Kelly Burn, and Glenna all carry prominent or mid-division inclinations but none projects as a genuine pace rival, meaning Kissmehoneyhoney will set a rhythm entirely to her own liking without being pressured into overdoing it. This lack of contested early fractions will compress the field, keep the tempo honest rather than searching, and likely produce a race where position off the turn rather than late raw finishing speed is decisive. A sustainable, uncontested pace over a stiff 1m4f Goodwood track strongly favours prominent-to-midfield racers who can sit close to the pace without being extravagant early and still have fuel for the climb to the line — hold-up horses depending on a strong gallop to reel in leaders will find this shape least accommodating, and the redistribution of Pierpoint and Cracking Beauty into midfield on the map reflects that the field contains more genuine closers than the pace structure will reward, with Ammoony, Kelly Burn, and Glenna best placed to benefit from their natural proximity to proceedings.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Kissmehoneyhoney is allowed to stride off cleanly and set a controlled, even pace that nobody seriously challenges.
scenarios.body: She settles into a rhythm, covers the Goodwood undulations well, and the lack of early pressure means she hits the rising ground to the finish with energy in reserve; her Goodwood form (second at the track over this sort of trip) and William Haggas handling are both relevant positives.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ammoony or Kelly Burn track Kissmehoneyhoney closely enough to exploit her the moment she flattens out approaching the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Both horses have course form at Goodwood and have been racing over 10-12f regularly, giving them the fitness and positional sharpness to pounce on a front-runner who has done all the donkey work; Kelly Burn's win at this exact course and distance is an obvious angle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely stronger than expected and the front ranks come back to the field in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Liveinthelight has won three of her last four and has strong Goodwood course form over 12f, giving her a live squeak if the run of the race suits late delivery; Marianita and Mother Dear are less exposed but have not shown the form to make them credible unless conditions fall perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Splits The Race
scenarios.trigger: If there is a notable incident early, a false start scenario, or Kissmehoneyhoney misses the break and the pace dynamics scramble into unpredictability.
scenarios.body: Without the expected leader at the head of affairs, the race becomes a much more attritional and tactical affair where form lines count for less; in that muddled shape, Glenna's versatility and Cracking Beauty's consistency at 3f+ trips become marginal factors.

watchPoints.text: Kissmehoneyhoney's early break and stride is the race-defining moment — if she misses the start or is restrained, the entire pace architecture collapses and the race becomes genuinely open.

Kelly Burn has been off 63 days and her prominent style means she needs to travel smoothly from the outset; if she dwells or races lazily after the layoff she could use up energy compensating for lost early ground on this stiff track.

Liveinthelight is on a hat-trick of wins and is the most in-form horse in the race, but watch whether Kieran Shoemark can find a position close enough to the pace — if she is too far back with a controlled gallop ahead, her finishing kick has nothing meaningful to attack.

Ammoony steps up to 1m4f for the first time today; watch how she travels through the middle stages, as any sign of laboured movement beyond a mile would indicate the trip is stretching her and would benefit those already proven over the distance.|

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm for this 1m4f slot — monitor whether any significant drying during the afternoon session tightens conditions further, which could sharpen the advantage for those proven on quicker ground such as Liveinthelight and Kelly Burn.|

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ruby's Profit
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who goes in hood and tongue-tie, with five Goodwood runs providing intimate course knowledge; faces direct early competition from Grandlad and the contested pace may drain her finish, though Tom Marquand's big-race experience is a positive factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Ruby's Profit nonetheless shapes as the chief threat here — ranked top of the field on our ratings, she brings strong fitness from a run just 14 days ago and has experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that elusive win remains stubbornly out of reach.

runners_data.name: Grandlad
runners_data.note: Three wins and four placed efforts from his last ten similar-going runs tell you he handles these conditions; a regular Goodwood front-runner who has won over this exact 5f course, James Horton's yard in fair 14-day form, but battling Ruby's Profit for the lead could prove costly late.
runners_data.comment: Grandlad won four starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions pose no unknown, and he arrives fresh on 17 days' rest carrying 138 lb from stall 5; the risk is that his last three runs have all returned sixth or seventh.

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with outstanding Goodwood form — placed on four of five attempts at the course including two podiums at 5f — and Harry Davies in the plate keeps costs down without sacrificing competence; a true-run race is exactly what his profile needs.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Bullet shaped well when third two starts back and ran a cracking race to finish second last time out, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead; the concern is whether he can convert that consistency into a win off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Brave Nation
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who won at Goodwood 5f on his most recent start and has placed there again since; Kieren Fox gets a clear tactical brief to sit and wait, and the solid similar-going record of 11/15 suggests the ground holds no fears at all.
runners_data.comment: Brave Nation arrives on the back of a win last time out and returns in good heart after 20 days, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; carrying 136 lb from stall four, he makes plenty of appeal.

runners_data.name: Silver Wraith
runners_data.note: Three near-misses in six Goodwood appearances but yet to win here; Saffie Osborne navigates a field of nine with the horse's hold-up style suiting a strongly-run race, though the 0W from 11 similar-going runs flags a certain vulnerability when it matters most.
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back shows she retains ability, but three of her last six have been unplaced and she arrives on the back of a disappointing effort; has run over today's trip and going, and 133 lb is no gimme, though a rating of 77 keeps her in contention from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: A hold-up type by style who has built a consistent string of placed efforts at Goodwood, and the short 8-day turnaround with Grace Harris's yard in form (5/15) suggests readiness; Ashley Lewis's 3lb claim is a notable asset at the weights.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Over Spiced faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick turnaround just eight days since her last outing.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has struggled for a clear winning chance in recent Goodwood starts, with David Egan booked and a 1/6 trainer 14-day record that is modest; respectable course form at 5f but the 0W from 11 similar-going runs limits confidence in a winning outcome.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Kiss And Run heads to the tape just 11 days after her latest effort and has experience of today's distance and going, which helps her cause; however, a rated mark of 68 and a run of mid-to-back-field finishes suggest she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Sandscreendeliverd
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator by nature who wears a hood; mapped here to midfield because the field holds more rear-runners than can all find their natural position — racing without a clear run to the back of the field will compromise its effectiveness, and the 0/2 trainer 14-day record offers little support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sandscreendeliverd has experience of today's trip and going but was beaten into eighth last time and ranks seventh of nine on our figures, making him difficult to fancy despite a modest weight and draw two.

runners_data.name: Velvet Goldmine
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3-year-old with only three runs but already placed twice at Goodwood, suggesting genuine affinity for the course; the 76-day absence is the key unknown, but Kieran Shoemark's Goodwood expertise and the Ed Walker yard's class could see it step forward fresh if it finds a clean prominent berth.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Velvet Goldmine faces a stiff task here after 76 days off, though she has run over today's distance and going before, and placed efforts of second and third in recent starts suggest she retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Ruby's Profit and Grandlad are both confirmed front-runners who will clash for the lead from the off on this straight 5f Goodwood track, creating a genuinely contested pace that should ensure an honest, even gallop throughout. Ruby's Profit has course form and goes in hood and tongue-tie, while Grandlad has won here at 5f and will not surrender the lead cheaply, meaning neither is likely to get a soft time in front. This contested dynamic classically sets up for closers and prominent horses to benefit from a true-run race, with horses like Rogue Bullet — who has strong course form and a prominent style — ideally positioned to exploit a frantic early battle. The race shape distinctly favours horses racing just off the pace or from midfield who can conserve energy through the first two furlongs before unleashing their finish; the field also contains more hold-up types than can comfortably slot to the rear, with Sandscreendeliverd mapped to midfield despite being a true hold-up horse, meaning it is unlikely to get its preferred position and its chance should be tempered accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ruby's Profit and Grandlad battle hard from the front and the prominent-style horses time their runs to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off setting a genuine pace, leaving the race wide open for a horse sitting just off them to cruise into contention around the 2f marker; Rogue Bullet's excellent course form and prominent style make it the primary beneficiary, with Brave Nation's proven Goodwood record also giving it a live chance late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Softly
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners edges clear early and the other fails to sustain the challenge, allowing the leader to coast at their own pace.
scenarios.body: Ruby's Profit or Grandlad gets a clear advantage inside the first furlong and is allowed to set a comfortable tempo, giving them enough in reserve to kick clear again when challenged; horses without early pace will find it hard to close once the race is run more steadily in the middle portion.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely scorching and the front two tie each other up completely, leaving the field strung out and the rear-runners with ground to make up.
scenarios.body: A furiously-run early tempo sees Ruby's Profit and Grandlad flatten each other before the 2f pole, opening the door for horses with a proven turn of foot to close rapidly; Silver Wraith, who has shown near-miss form at Goodwood, and Over Spiced, with several placed efforts at this course, are best-placed to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Youngster Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner battle creates positional chaos and a lightly-raced horse is allowed to slot into an uncontested prominent position.
scenarios.body: Velvet Goldmine, with only three runs and strong placed form at Goodwood already, could find an uncluttered berth just off the battle and produce an unexposed turn of foot at a sharp price; the 3-year-old's consistent form figures on this course and the Kieran Shoemark booking add to the intrigue despite the 76-day break.

watchPoints.text: Ruby's Profit and Grandlad will directly contest the lead from the stalls — watch for either horse being pushed wider or losing position in the first furlong, as whoever blinks first could find their race effectively over by halfway.
Velvet Goldmine is 76 days absent and has had only three career starts; watch the paddock for any signs of freshness or lack of work fitness before committing to it as a pace beneficiary.

Sandscreendeliverd's natural hold-up style will be compromised by the number of closers in this field — watch whether Pat Dobbs attempts to push forward early, which would be a clear sign the horse is being ridden against its grain.

The going is officially Good To Firm at Goodwood's 5f course today — watch for any late market moves on horses with form in faster conditions, as the quicker underfoot will suit horses with a clean, low action over this straight course.

Over Spiced runs just 8 days after its last start — watch early to see if it travels smoothly and settles, as a quick turnaround on Good To Firm ground at 5f can expose any residual fatigue in the back straight.

races.name: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose two wins at Goodwood over 6f on similar ground are the standout credentials here; Toby Moore claims 7lbs, and at 30 days since last run connections appear to have targeted this race, though he needs a stronger pace than Veil Of Clouds is likely to set.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and rated below his official mark, Rory Rocket faces a stiff ask, though he does bring distance and going experience, returns from a fair 30-day break, and his record includes three wins in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Raffles Angel
runners_data.note: Course and distance specialist with three placings at Goodwood in recent runs and an excellent sim-going record of 12 qualifiers; Hector Crouch takes over and this prominent-running five-year-old should slot in behind the leader naturally, giving her every chance to challenge late.|
runners_data.comment: Raffles Angel has placed third twice in recent starts yet remains winless in her last five, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, 137 lb from stall seven is a stiff ask for a mare ranked sixth in this field.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Harry Davies can dictate unchallenged from gate to line; ran at Goodwood on her most recent start though finished fifth, and her tongue tie may help settle her; Simon and Ed Crisford are 4/18 over 14 days suggesting active form.|
runners_data.comment: Veil Of Clouds won last time out and arrives here just 11 days later in cracking shape, her trainer firing at 30% over the past fortnight and her experience over today's trip and going a further plus; the main risk is that 137 lb from stall 10 tests her.

runners_data.name: Perfect Location
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won at Sandown on soft and placed at Sandown on Good To Firm, giving some confidence on a range of surfaces; Rob Hornby takes over and the 46-day absence is the main query, though headgear switch (hood) could sharpen her early.|
runners_data.comment: Perfect Location won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid profile stepping back to familiar conditions; carrying 135 lb from stall nine after a 46-day break is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has placed twice at Goodwood over this exact course and distance in recent starts, making him a natural fit track-wise; Tom Marquand is a strong booking and the visor is retained, though his trainer has had no winners in the past 14 days from six runs.|
runners_data.comment: Northcliff catches the eye on his recent profile, finishing second in each of his last two starts and returning here just 14 days later in good heart; he has run over today's trip and going before, and he breaks from stall two under 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Newsreader
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by style — despite appearing in the midfield map, his natural position is at the rear and he races partially out of role here; David Egan cannot manufacture ground he needs if the pace is controlled, and his sim-going record shows just one placing from 15 starts.|
runners_data.comment: Newsreader has run over today's trip and going, lines up fresh on 24 days' rest, and our rating of 75 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 68 implies — yet he remains winless in his last five starts, and that consistency concern is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Sound And Vision
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has run all five of her turf starts at Goodwood or Sandown and holds two placings on Good To Firm course form, yet all her runs have come at 5f — stepping up to 6f is an unproven stamina question despite her hold-up style suiting a stronger gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Sound And Vision faces a stiff task, though she does bring distance and going experience and drew stall one; a winner in her last five starts, she was third two runs back and runner-up last time out, suggesting some consistency.

runners_data.name: Dark Alley
runners_data.note: Placed twice at Goodwood over 6f in recent outings on Good To Firm, which is the most relevant positive angle; a natural hold-up horse shown in midfield because the rear is overcrowded, so Edward Greatrex will need to find a way through if the tempo is slow, which dilutes his prospects.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dark Alley at least showed renewed life with a runner-up finish last time out — just 15 days ago — and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 129 lb burden from stall five, however, may blunt his chance of going one better.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Charles Bishop rides this Eve Johnson Houghton three-year-old who has run six recent starts all at Goodwood or similar tracks; consistent without winning, she sits prominently and the sim-going record of seven qualifiers suggests she handles conditions, but she needs to find another gear she has not shown at OR 67.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with his form deteriorating recently — four, fifth and sixth in his last three outings — Eightthreeone faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures, and a trainer striking at just three per cent over the past fortnight offers little encouragement, despite his having run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ararat
runners_data.note: A six-year-old who has been running at 7f-8f in recent starts for Rachel Cook and John Bridger — dropping back to 6f may sharpen his speed, but his natural closing style is compromised by the crowded back-end of this field, and the short trainer strike rate of 1/6 over 14 days offers little confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ararat does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 73 suggests more ability than his official mark of 63 implies; however, a run of 6th last time out and nothing better than third in recent starts makes him hard to anchor at the head of affairs from stall six.

races.paceDynamic: Veil Of Clouds is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Harry Davies can dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front on the Good To Firm ground at Goodwood's straight six. Raffles Angel and Perfect Location will push forward to dispute the early prominent positions, with Eightthreeone also likely to sit just off them, creating a compact, organised front group rather than a combustive pace duel. The field contains more hold-up inclination than the map can accommodate — Newsreader, Dark Alley, and Ararat are genuine closers by nature but are redistributed into the midfield picture because the rear is already congested with similar types, meaning their true finishing positions may be further forward than ideal and their effectiveness is compromised. With Veil Of Clouds able to control tempo without pressure, a sustainable, front-running gallop is the dominant shape, and horses racing prominently or tracking the leader in the first three to four lengths will be best placed to capitalise on the Goodwood straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Veil Of Clouds Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Veil Of Clouds is allowed to dictate a measured tempo unchallenged and the prominent racers cannot close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Veil Of Clouds sets a sustainable pace on Good To Firm ground that suits her natural front-running style, and with no horse applying genuine early pressure, she can conserve enough energy to hold on close home; horses positioned prominently or just off the pace have the best chance of running her down if she does tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Her Back
scenarios.trigger: If Raffles Angel or Perfect Location push forward more aggressively than expected and force a stronger gallop, draining Veil Of Clouds late.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace lifts the tempo sufficiently to set up a genuine end-to-end test, and a horse travelling smoothly in the first three lengths with tactical cover — such as Raffles Angel with Good To Firm course experience — is ideally placed to pick off the leader in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finishers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a false early crawl sets up a sprint finish that scrambles the field and allows midfield horses to close.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo followed by a sharp acceleration in the final two furlongs could briefly open a gap for horses like Rory Rocket or Sound And Vision, both comfortable at Goodwood on similar ground, to finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong end to end and the front group tires, allowing the genuine hold-up horses to arrive from further back.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Newsreader, Dark Alley, or Ararat to overcome their redistributed positions — they are natural hold-up types forced out of their ideal role — and depends on a strong gallop that simply may not materialise with only one confirmed front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Raffles Angel or Perfect Location push forward to press Veil Of Clouds early — if either commits aggressively, the controlled front-running scenario unravels and the pace lifts markedly.|

Rory Rocket's two Goodwood 6f wins are the most specific course-and-distance credentials in the field; if Toby Moore (7lb claimer) times the run perfectly, he could arrive with a late charge that catches the eye.|

Sound And Vision is unproven beyond 5f — if she fades in the final furlong having tracked prominently, it signals the trip has found her out and will affect the shape of the finish for midfield runners behind her.|

Northcliff has placed twice consecutively over this exact course and distance in recent starts; if Tom Marquand tracks the leader in second or third, he is the most likely horse to capitalise if Veil Of Clouds weakens.|

The Good To Firm ground is confirmed for this race specifically in the going report — horses with a positive sim-going record at Goodwood on similar surfaces (Raffles Angel 12/15, Rory Rocket 7/15) hold a meaningful track-condition edge over those without course form.|

races.name: Gay Kindersley Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kimeko Glory
runners_data.note: Course winner at Goodwood (1/8f) and consistent on this track; wears blinkers which sharpen focus, but in this field she cannot get as far back as she ideally wants, compromising the late burst that defines her best form.
runners_data.comment: Kimeko Glory won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making her an obvious candidate to follow up; the weight of 159 lb from stall nine is the one factor to monitor, but her recent form puts her clear at the head of this field.

runners_data.name: Show Biz Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong Goodwood course record (won 1/10f here) and solid strike rate in similar going; 29 days since last run is fine, and if pace is genuine he can deliver a clean late challenge from a honest midfield berth.
runners_data.comment: Show Biz Kid has run over today's trip and going, and his third two starts back shows he can get competitive, though fifth last time out and a win four starts back suggest inconsistency; 156 lb is no gimme, but 29 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has four top-five finishes from five Goodwood runs over this trip, showing the track suits; hold-up style means he needs things to fall right, but his consistency here makes him a legitimate place contender if pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Beach Point arrives on the back of a consistent string of fourths, with his one recent placing — third five starts back — highlighting his knack for running well without quite getting his head in front, and our rating of 75 puts him right in the mix; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: Remarkably in-form — three wins in last five starts including two over 1m2f on Good — though today is shorter at 1m1f; Miss Brodie Hampson is an amateur but Pride Of Nepal's front-running-adjacent prominent style means he doesn't need the jockey to ride a waiting game.
runners_data.comment: Pride Of Nepal has tumbled down the order in his last two starts after a four-timer, and our figures rank him ninth of ten here, making him hard to fancy at the weights off 69; the step back to familiar distance and going offers some hope, but he needs to rediscover that winning thread sharpish.

runners_data.name: Gone Rogue
runners_data.note: Two wins over this course and distance (1/8f GOO, 1/10f GOO) give him the strongest course profile in the race; prominent style positions him perfectly to sit just behind the front-runners and strike when they weaken, making him the cleanest stylistic fit for the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Gone Rogue brings a sharp profile to this contest, winning last time out and again three starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main risk is whether he can defy a burden of 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Sant Alessio
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who won over 8f at Goodwood and will look to dominate from flag to finish; 58 days off is a mild query, and trainer has a flat 0/3 in the last 14 days, but his role as pace-setter makes him pivotal regardless of his own winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Sant Alessio showed a win four starts back and a second five starts back, but he has been largely out of the picture since, finishing unplaced, seventh, and fourth in his last three; now 58 days off the track, fitness is the question as he shoulders 154 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Romantic Spirit
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter who will contest the early lead with Sant Alessio; however, recent form is a string of 4-5-7-7-7 mostly on Soft-Standard, and this is only the horse's first run on genuinely fast ground, making it hard to trust for more than pace-making duties.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and without a finish better than fourth in recent form, Romantic Spirit at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, though 62 days off and 152 lb from stall five make this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Grey Fox
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with two placed runs at Goodwood (2nd and 3rd over 10f) showing the track is very much in his favour; races as a true hold-up type but with this many hold-up horses in the field he is forced forward, which sits against his natural comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Grey Fox arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second two starts back, but had finished sixth and sixth before that, and his ranking of eighth of ten on our figures makes him a tough sell carrying 151 lb from stall ten, winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Platinum Prince
runners_data.note: Blinkers on, consistent place-getter (2nd and 4th in last five), and trainer Gary & Josh Moore are in form (2/21 in 14 days); however, at 9 years old and 51 days since last run, and operating as a genuine rear-of-field type squeezed into midfield here, winning conditions are demanding.
runners_data.comment: Platinum Prince has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 75 suggests he is better than his official mark of 63 implies, giving him a lively each-way chance from stall 8; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 51 days off.

runners_data.name: Artavian
runners_data.note: Drops sharply in class on OR 54 with a tongue-tie and visor combination suggesting connections are searching for a gear; has placed twice at 10f on Soft but this is his first run on Good To Firm, and amateur jockey Mr Frederick Tett adds uncertainty to an already underpowered profile on paper.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Artavian has little obvious appeal here, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and a run twenty days ago leaves him fit enough.

races.paceDynamic: Sant Alessio and Romantic Spirit are the two confirmed front-runners in this 10-runner 1m1f handicap on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood, and with both likely to want the early lead, the opening stages should see a genuinely contested gallop rather than anything dawdling. Sant Alessio has course-winning form over shorter and will want to dominate, while Romantic Spirit has shown consistent prominent intent despite modest recent form, creating a dynamic where neither will yield cheaply in the first two furlongs. The resulting honest, even pace over Goodwood's undulating track is likely to suit horses who can sit just off the speed in the prominent-to-midfield bracket and pick off weakening leaders in the home straight — Gone Rogue and Pride Of Nepal are best positioned to exploit that shape. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Kimeko Glory, Grey Fox, and Platinum Prince are genuine hold-up horses pushed into a midfield representation, with Sant Alessio and Romantic Spirit the only runners realistically securing the early front positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sant Alessio or Romantic Spirit sets an honest gallop that strings the field and Gone Rogue or Pride Of Nepal track close enough to pounce.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace burns off the true hold-up horses who can't get close enough, while a prominent stalker swoops in the final furlong on the downhill run to the line; Gone Rogue's two wins over this course and distance make him the standout beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Sant Alessio — dominates unchallenged after the other fails to sustain pressure and builds an unassailable lead.
scenarios.body: Sant Alessio's course-winning pedigree and front-running style could allow him to control tempo and ration his effort, leaving the hold-up horses with too much ground to recover; on Good To Firm ground the pace could be sustainable enough for a well-judged front-running display.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too hard early and burn each other out, opening the door for runners tracking in midfield to sweep past in the straight.
scenarios.body: Show Biz Kid and Beach Point, sitting honest mid-division with genuine Goodwood course form, would be best placed to capitalise on a pace collapse; however this scenario is modestly discounted because the redistributed hold-up horses (Kimeko Glory, Grey Fox, Platinum Prince) mapped here are not truly comfortable racing this prominently and may not deliver their finish from this position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If a slow early crawl develops — unlikely given two front-runners — allowing genuine hold-up horses to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Kimeko Glory has blinkers and solid Goodwood form but is racing out of her natural position in this competitive shape, and Grey Fox's two recent Goodwood places suggest ability; both are nonetheless significantly disadvantaged by the pace dynamic that prevents them settling as far back as they prefer.

watchPoints.text: Gone Rogue has won twice over this exact course and trip in similar going — if he settles just behind the front-runners he is the single most dangerous horse in the race for the dominant scenario.

Sant Alessio and Romantic Spirit are both genuine front-runners and neither is likely to yield: watch the opening two furlongs for a contested lead that could compromise both their winning chances if they burn too hard.

Pride Of Nepal arrives on the back of a hat-trick of wins but drops back from 1m2f and has not run on genuinely fast ground (only 7/15 sim-going matches) — if the pace is strong and the track rides quick, stamina reserve may thin out late.

Kimeko Glory, Grey Fox, and Platinum Prince are all natural hold-up horses unable to get their preferred position in this race — if any of them drift wide hunting cover early, it is a sign they are uncomfortable and their finishing kick may be compromised.

Romantic Spirit has raced exclusively on Standard-to-Soft ground at Lingfield and Kempton in recent starts; this is only his second recorded run on Good-type turf and the first on Good To Firm — a surface unknown is worth monitoring in running.
